qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.) — a real consecutive second-cycle degree, not a certificate
accreditationStatus: State-recognised public institution (Baden-Württemberg); consecutive accredited M.A. UNVERIFIED which agency
language: German. Minimum German level demanded: C1 ('Language of Instruction: German (minimum C1 level required)'). Accepted proofs listed: DSH, Goethe KDS/GDS or equivalent.
whatYouStudy: Consecutive popular-music master with three concentrations — Performing Artist, Producing/Composing Artist, Educating Artist. The Producing/Composing track is the record-making one: production, composition, arrangement, studio work across pop, rock, soul, reggae, punk, metal, techno, hip-hop.
entryRequirements: Verbatim per admission page: qualifying bachelor degrees are 'Pop Music Design or Music Business from the Popakademie Baden-Württemberg', 'Music (New Music, Classical, Jazz, Popular Music)', 'Music Education', 'Musicology', 'Literature (German, English)', 'Cultural Studies', 'Media-related Studies', 'Art and Design'. Programme 'targets university graduates who have practical experience in music at a high level'.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the qualifying list extends beyond music to 'Literature (German, English), Cultural Studies, Media-related Studies, Art and Design'. A BSc Software Engineering is NOT on that list and is very unlikely to qualify. The page also states the programme is for graduates 'who have practical experience in music at a high level'. Verdict for this candidate: effectively closed.
portfolioSpec: Pre-selection recording: '5 titles' for the Producing/Composing Artist concentration (3 titles for Performing/Educating Artist). FAQ adds that producers should submit 'productions that are as close to finished as possible' demonstrating musical breadth. Exact file format and per-track length: UNVERIFIED — not stated on the pages.
auditionSpec: BOTH a performance audition and written exams. Written exam: musical analysis (melody, harmony, rhythm, form, arrangement, production aspects) plus an essay on the history/aesthetics of popular music. Audition: 15-minute public performance of 3-5 compositions/covers, live or with playback, then ad-hoc accompaniment questions and a one-to-one interview. Oral exam: private discussion of motivation and qualifications. NOTE: this is a genuine performance audition, not a studio production test.
tuitionNonEU: €1,500 per semester = €3,000/year for non-EU/EEA students (Baden-Württemberg state non-EU tuition). Popakademie states 'there are no tuition fees for a consecutive master's programme' but immediately excepts 'some international students as well as those pursuing a second course of study'. The €1,500/semester figure is the standard Baden-Württemberg non-EU rate — UNVERIFIED against a Popakademie fee document.
totalCostEstimate: Approx. €3,000/year tuition plus roughly €11,000-12,000/year living costs in Mannheim (student visa blocked-account benchmark). UNVERIFIED as an official figure.
scholarships: No programme-specific scholarship confirmed. DAAD Study Scholarships for artists/musicians are the realistic external route. UNVERIFIED.
languageRequirement: German C1 (DSH, Goethe KDS/GDS or equivalent)
englishTest: Not applicable — programme taught in German
deadline: Application deadline 30 April; entrance exam 29-30 June. Dates confirmed for the 2026 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE — the September 2027 intake would mean applying by ~30 April 2027 with the exam in late June 2027, dates not yet published).

whatYouStudy: Audio direction for film and media — the creative lead role over sound design, music and mix. Grows out of the FH Dortmund B.A. Film & Sound.
entryRequirements: Verbatim in substance: admission requires 'a Diploma or Bachelor's degree in Film-Sound-Design/Film Music/Film-Sound-Engineer or a comparable media studies program at a university with sound as a study focus of at least 75% and with an overall grade of at least "good" (2.0)', comprising 'at least seven semesters or 210 ECTS credit points'. institution: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) jointly with TU Graz
program: Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur, Masterstudium (Electrical Engineering and Audio Engineering)
qualification: Diplom-Ingenieur/in (DI / Dipl.-Ing.) — a real second-cycle DEGREE, NOT a Universitätslehrgang. Study code UV 066 413.
accreditationStatus: Ordentliches Masterstudium at two Austrian public universities; curriculum published by KUG
language: German. Minimum German level demanded: 'Deutschkenntnisse Level C1/GERS', or admission at A2 with a subsequent supplementary German exam (Ergänzungsprüfung).
whatYouStudy: Inter-university Tonmeister/audio-engineering master combining electrical engineering and IT coursework with music practice, recording studio work, acoustics, audio signal processing and sound engineering. Taught jointly by TU Graz and KUG (home of the IEM).
entryRequirements: Verbatim: 'Studierende, die an der KUG/TU Graz das Bachelorstudium Elektrotechnik - Toningenieur abgeschlossen haben, erfüllen die Aufnahmevoraussetzungen.' External applicants need a 'gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigtes Studium' (equivalent qualifying prior degree); up to 30 additional ECTS from the bachelor programme may be prescribed. External applicants must also pass an admission examination and submit 'certificates of your musical-artistic background' to the KUG Studien- und Prüfungsabteilung by 30 June.
acceptsNonMusic: YES IN PRINCIPLE, conditionally. The rule is 'gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigtes Studium' judged by the dean, with 'up to 30 additional ECTS from the bachelor program may be required' — an engineering/computer-science bachelor is the natural equivalence route here, unlike the pure music schools. BUT the candidate must still pass the KUG artistic aptitude test and produce 'certificates of your musical-artistic background', which he does not have. This is the single most engineering-friendly entry in the DACH territory for a software-engineering BSc.
portfolioSpec: No track portfolio. Instead: bachelor transcript/diploma plus certificates of musical-artistic background, submitted to KUG by 30 June.
auditionSpec: APTITUDE TEST, not a performance audition and not a production test. Three written components: (1) Seashore Test, ~40 min — discrimination of frequency, intensity and duration, plus timbre and rhythm memory; (2) Ear Training Test, ~20 min — melodic and rhythmic dictation, interval, chord and instrument recognition; (3) Music Theory Test, ~15 min — intervals, scales, rhythm notation. Held online.
tuitionNonEU: Austrian public-university non-EU rate applies: €726.72 per semester = €1,453.44/year. UNVERIFIED against a KUG fee page — confirm with KUG Studienabteilung.
otherFees: ÖH-Beitrag (student union) ~€25-26 per semester plus insurance. UNVERIFIED exact current amount.
totalCostEstimate: Approx. €1,450/year tuition plus Graz living costs; Austrian student residence permit requires proof of roughly €12,000-13,000/year. UNVERIFIED as official figures.
scholarships: Austrian Grants (OeAD) / Ernst Mach Grant are the usual external routes for non-EU students. No programme-specific scholarship confirmed. UNVERIFIED.
deadline: Documents to KUG by 30 June; application to the admission exam by 3 June, exam 27 June (dates shown for the 2027 exam cycle on the KUG page — treat as indicative, reconfirm). Study starts winter semester.
